library.description: Runtime-neutral transient event subscription and fan-out primitives.

blocks.text: English
`@migaia/event-subscriber` 把本地事件分发给一组监听器，并为等待结果、取消订阅和精确选择一个处理者提供明确规则。

items: 界面先显示新值，又跳回旧值：第一个回调发布新事件时，递归派发抢在当前轮其余回调之前执行。
监听器漏收到一次，或新订阅提前收到旧事件：发布过程直接遍历正在被增删的回调数组。
离开页面后旧组件继续收到更新：请求用了取消信号，事件订阅却没有绑定到相同寿命。
一个处理者失败，其他成功数据也丢了：把事件通知当成能等待全部结果的异步调用，却没有逐项结算。
一次保存写入两次：重复挂载建立了两个同名处理者，调用前没有检查目标是否唯一。
嵌套更新按轮次交付。 手写递归广播会让新值插入旧值这一轮；显式 queued 策略先完成当前快照（发布开始时固定的接收者列表），示例依次展示 1、2。
订阅增删不改变当前接收者。 遍历活动数组容易漏调用或多调用；入口快照固定本轮目标，示例把新增订阅留到第二轮。
取消信号同时管住事件订阅。 手写取消代码容易只停请求、漏掉监听器；`subscribeUntil` 既退订事件也移除信号监听，示例取消后剩余登记为零。
失败不会抹掉并行成功值。 只处理整体拒绝容易丢失已成功结果；`invokeParallelSettled` 按登记顺序返回各自的成功值或失败，示例保留成功值 6。
命令目标不唯一时先拒绝执行。 直接广播或取首个匹配会重复写入或掩盖重复登记；`invokeTask` 在调用前要求恰好一个匹配，示例的第二次尝试没有再次保存。

blocks.text: 用 Node 24 直接运行。第一个监听器处理值 1 时又发布值 2；排队交付让第二个监听器先看到 1，再看到 2。
输出：

blocks.code:
记录: 1
展示: 1
记录: 2
展示: 2

blocks.text: 遇到页面退订看取消信号，需要等待处理结果看并行结算。
下面仅展示，不运行。它用原生数组管理与上一节相同的嵌套更新。
上一节由 channel 先固定目标，再用显式 queued 策略完成当前轮；不用在每个监听器里手写重入协调。默认策略仍是 recursive，需要这种顺序时应明确选择 queued。

blocks.code: pnpm add @migaia/event-subscriber

blocks.text: 根入口负责 channel、Hub 与调用工具；独立订阅 helper 从 `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber` 导入。运行时只依赖 `@migaia/utils`，没有 DOM 或 Node 依赖，`sideEffects: false`。

rows: 创建单事件通道，固定每轮接收者与重入策略。
按事件名和对应 payload 类型路由本地通知。
把订阅寿命绑定到取消信号。
并行等待每个监听器，保留成功与失败。
等前一个结束后再调用下一个。
执行前确认 `taskId` 恰好匹配一个登记。

blocks.text: `createEventChannel<T, R>()` 中，`T` 是发布载荷类型，`R` 是监听器结果类型。指定结果类型不会改变 channel 的订阅模型，也不会创建全局任务表。

基础订阅有两种签名：`subscribe(listener, options?: { taskId?: string; delivery?: 'context' }): subscription` 保留事件上下文，原始载荷放在 `event.value`；`subscribe(listener, options: { taskId?: string; delivery: 'value' }): subscription` 把原始 payload 直接交给监听器。
公开选项类型为 `IEventSubscribeOptions`，模式常量为 `EventDelivery.context`、`EventDelivery.value`。可选的 `taskId` 是调用方给本次登记起的标签；返回的 `subscription` 负责取消并可追加订阅。
只处理 payload 时可显式选择 value：

value 模式保持 payload 身份，不提供 `abort()`、`setTaskId()` 或 `taskId` 上下文成员；登记时的 `taskId` 仍可用于任务过滤。需要上下文控制或 `valueConfig` 别名时保留默认 context。通道订阅链、命名别名及 Hub 的第三个订阅参数都接受相同的 delivery 选择；Hub 不接受任务标签。`subscribeOnce`、`subscribeUntil` 仍只接收上下文监听器。
动态事件名可在运行时广播；有限字面量事件表的同一条链禁止重复事件名。这是 TypeScript 的订阅链类型约束；另一条独立链仍可订阅同名事件。
默认采用同步 recursive 派发、multiple 登记、handle 级取消、每次顶层发布 `100_000` 次调用预算和非严格的已取消信号准入。监听器增删、clear 和任务改标签不改变当前快照；每次之后的调用重新选择目标。
同步 `publish()` 不等待 Promise。同步抛错收集为 `PUBLISH_FAILED`，迟到拒绝交给 report；异步调用工具等待结算，通过返回值或拒绝交付结果。settled 只收集监听器失败，通道与任务准入错误仍同步抛出。
`invokeParallelSettled(channel, payload)` 按登记顺序返回结算项：`{ status: 'fulfilled', value }` 的 `value` 是监听器兑现后的返回值；`{ status: 'rejected', reason }` 的 `reason` 是监听器原始的抛错或拒绝原因。这些字段描述监听器执行结果，不是消息发送回执。
订阅句柄可以串联，并按相反顺序、幂等地取消；关闭后不能追加。静态 `valueConfig` 只为 context 模式的上下文附加一个路径值，不转换事件或 value 监听器的 payload。

设置 `style: 'on-emit'` 后，`channel.on(listener)` 登记监听器并返回本次订阅的句柄，`channel.emit(value)` 按所选派发策略把 value 交给当前快照中的监听器。默认 handle 取消策略下，句柄的 `off()` 只移除它拥有的登记。`on`、`emit`、`off` 分别与 `subscribe`、`publish`、`unsubscribe` 指向同一函数；canonical（固定原名）方法仍保留。

从 `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber` 导入的 `subscribeOnce`、`subscribeUntil`、`subscribeSubscriber` 只通过 `channel.subscribe(listener, options?)` 工作，不读取 style 配置，因此可以接收仍保留该方法的 styled channel（增加命名别名的通道）。它们的返回值固定为普通 `IUnsubscribe`，即同步、幂等的取消函数，不带 `off`、`dispose`、`unlisten` 或订阅链方法。

对象订阅者只需实现 `IEventSubscriber<T, R>` 的 `handle(event)`，事件来源由 `subscribeSubscriber(channel, subscriber)` 中的 channel 决定；多事件名称由 Hub 的 `subscribe(key, listener)` 中的 key 决定。旧草案中的抽象类 `EventSubscriber`、静态 `EVENT_NAME` 与 `onCall()` 不属于当前公开契约，不把事件名重复存进 class。
Hub 的内部策略固定为上述默认值，不接受单通道策略配置。它不聚合监听器结果；需要返回值时使用带结果类型的 channel。
事件是瞬时通知，不提供当前值、重放、跨进程传输、资源宿主、排空或背压。完整参数、命名风格、静态值路径、19 个错误码和构建命令见使用指南。
English
先按场景查找，再读完整契约。安装包后，每个运行示例都能单独保存为 `.ts` 文件，用 Node 24 直接运行；代码与对应网站场景一致。包的选用依据见 README。

sections.id: 让嵌套通知等当前这一轮交付完成
sections.heading: 让嵌套通知等当前这一轮交付完成

blocks.text: 处理更新的监听者又发布一次更新，其余监听者还没有收到第一条。手写递归回调会让页面先看到新事件，又被旧事件覆盖。排队交付（`queued`）策略先完成当前这一轮的登记快照，再交付嵌套的值；两轮都在同一次同步 `publish` 调用内完成。
输出：

blocks.code:
记录: 1
展示: 1
记录: 2
展示: 2

blocks.text: 依次输出 `记录: 1`、`展示: 1`、`记录: 2`、`展示: 2`。嵌套事件没有插入当前这一轮。默认策略是 `recursive`，排队交付需要显式选择 `queued`。

sections.id: 修改订阅时不打乱当前交付
sections.heading: 修改订阅时不打乱当前交付

blocks.text: 交付事件时，一个监听者移除另一条订阅，又登记新的监听者。直接遍历可变回调数组容易漏掉原有接收者，或让新订阅意外收到当前事件。`publish` 先取得一份登记快照：增删作用于后续发布，当前快照仍按登记顺序执行。
输出：

blocks.code: 首位 1 | 次位 1 | 首位 2 | 新增 2

blocks.text: 输出 `首位 1 | 次位 1 | 首位 2 | 新增 2`。退订没有让次位监听者漏掉第一轮；新登记从第二次发布才开始收到事件。

sections.id: 离开页面时一起退订多个事件
sections.heading: 离开页面时一起退订多个事件

blocks.text: 页面同时监听保存和关闭事件，清理时漏掉一个事件名，旧页面就会继续收到更新。带事件映射类型的 hub 为不同事件保留各自的参数类型；把页面的登记串在同一条订阅链上，一个句柄就能按相反顺序全部退订。
输出：

blocks.code:
已保存: order-1
已关闭: 详情页
剩余订阅: 0

blocks.text: 依次输出 `已保存: order-1`、`已关闭: 详情页`、`剩余订阅: 0`。页面清理后的发布没有输出；一个句柄移除了整条链上的登记。

sections.id: 页面取消后不再接收更新
sections.heading: 页面取消后不再接收更新

blocks.text: 组件用一个 `AbortController` 管理操作，离开页面时却漏掉了事件订阅。手写取消监听既要退订事件，也要清理取消监听本身。`subscribeUntil` 把登记绑定到信号，同时返回可重复调用的手动退订函数，供提前清理。
输出：

blocks.code:
展示: 已保存
剩余订阅: 0

blocks.text: 输出 `展示: 已保存`，然后是 `剩余订阅: 0`。取消移除了后续交付；之后再调用 `stop` 没有副作用。已经执行中的监听者不会被打断；传入已取消的信号时，默认不建立登记。

sections.id: 一个监听者失败时仍保留其他结果
sections.heading: 一个监听者失败时仍保留其他结果

blocks.text: 导出操作同时向多个处理者索取结果。只处理一个整体拒绝时，成功返回的数据容易被一起丢掉。`invokeParallelSettled` 立即启动快照里的监听者，按登记顺序保留每个成功值或原始失败原因；传入非法 `channel` 的准入错误仍会同步抛出。
输出：

blocks.code:
成功: 6
失败: 远端暂不可用

blocks.text: 输出 `成功: 6`，然后是 `失败: 远端暂不可用`。第二个监听者先失败，但结果数组仍按登记顺序排列，成功值没有丢失。

sections.id: 前一个处理者结束后再运行下一个
sections.heading: 前一个处理者结束后再运行下一个

blocks.text: 前一个异步写入尚未完成，通知就开始发送了，因为 `publish` 不等待监听者返回的 `Promise`。`invokeSerial` 等一个快照监听者结束后才启动下一个；它们都收到同一个输入，不会接收前一个的返回值。示例用日志模拟写入和通知。
输出：

blocks.code:
写入: order-1
写入完成
通知: order-1
结果: 已写入,已通知

blocks.text: 依次输出 `写入: order-1`、`写入完成`、`通知: order-1`、`结果: 已写入,已通知`。这只控制顺序，不是事务：某个监听者失败不会跳过后续监听者，全部执行后才汇总失败。

sections.id: 执行前拒绝重复登记的命令目标
sections.heading: 执行前拒绝重复登记的命令目标

blocks.text: 命令本来只应调用一个保存处理者，重复挂载却登记了两次，导致重复写入。`invokeTask` 在执行任何监听者之前按 `taskId` 选择唯一登记：名称不存在时同步抛 `TASK_NOT_FOUND`，重复匹配时同步抛 `TASK_NOT_UNIQUE`，此次不会调用任何处理者，其他任务名也不会被执行。
输出：

blocks.code:
保存结果: 3
重复目标: TASK_NOT_UNIQUE
保存调用次数: 1

blocks.text: 依次输出 `保存结果: 3`、`重复目标: TASK_NOT_UNIQUE`、`保存调用次数: 1`。第二次选择不唯一时没有再次保存。被选中的监听者失败时，以 `PUBLISH_FAILED` 拒绝并保留原始错误。

根入口 `@migaia/event-subscriber` 提供 channel、Hub、调用工具、常量与公开类型。子入口 `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber` 提供 `subscribeOnce`、`subscribeUntil`、`subscribeSubscriber` 和对应订阅类型。运行时只依赖 `@migaia/utils`，不依赖 DOM 或 Node；包标记为 `sideEffects: false`。

channel（事件通道）只分发当前发布的事件，不保存当前值，也不重放历史。registration（订阅登记）是一次订阅及其取消句柄。snapshot（快照）是一次发布开始时固定的目标列表。需要当前值或派生依赖时使用 `@migaia/reactive`；需要前一步结果传给下一步的中间件时使用 `@migaia/middleware-pipeline`；资源释放、队列和背压由 `@migaia/lifecycle` 或 `@migaia/resource` 负责；跨 Worker、窗口或网络的消息由 `@migaia/rpc-host` 加传输 plugin 负责。

sections.heading: 创建 channel 与完整参数

blocks.text: `createEventChannel<T, R, S, V>(options?)` 创建一个通道。`T` 是发布值类型，`R` 是监听器结果类型，默认 `void`；`S` 是命名风格，`V` 是静态值路径配置，两者默认 `undefined`。公开选项类型为 `IEventChannelOptions<T, S, V>`。只服务于类型推导的投影类型，以发布的声明和编辑器提示为准。

rows: 接收 `{ event, error }`。主要处理同步 `publish()` 返回后的监听器拒绝，也接收值路径诊断；可以同步返回或返回 Promise。缺省时进入终端诊断。同步监听器抛错由 `publish()` 聚合，不交给它。
接收诊断错误；`report` 缺失、抛错或异步拒绝时使用。可以同步返回或返回 Promise，失败会继续交给宿主诊断。
`'recursive'` 立即递归交付监听器内部的新发布；`'queued'` 等当前快照全部调用后再交付重入值。对应常量为 `EventDispatchPolicy.recursive`、`queued`。
`'multiple'` 每次订阅创建独立登记；`'unique'` 按同一监听器函数的身份只保留一份登记。对应 `EventAdmissionPolicy.multiple`、`unique`。
`'handle'` 只解除当前句柄拥有的登记；`'listener-all'` 解除同一监听器函数在该通道上的全部登记。对应 `EventRemovalPolicy.handle`、`listenerAll`。
一次顶层同步发布及其嵌套发布最多调用多少个监听器，必须是正安全整数。耗尽后停止展开，抛 `PUBLISH_FAILED`；`error.detail` 记录已处理数和剩余预算。
`false` 时，`subscribeUntil` 使用已取消信号不会登记，返回空操作取消函数；`true` 时同步抛 `ABORTED` 的 `TypeError`。
仅给已有操作增加方法别名。四个预设与自定义字段见下文，不改变派发或取消语义。
未配置时不增加值别名。配置固定的 `readPath`、`alias` 字段，规则见“静态值路径”。

blocks.text: `options` 必须是对象，不能为 `null` 或数组；非法选项为 `INVALID_OPTIONS`。`report` 或 `terminalReport` 提供后必须可调用，否则为 `INVALID_REPORTER`。读取选项的 getter 抛错时，原始失败保留在错误链上。

sections.id: 通道方法与事件上下文
sections.heading: 通道方法与事件上下文

rows: 按登记顺序添加监听器，返回可调用、可链式扩展的句柄。默认 `listener(event)` 接收下面的上下文；显式 `delivery: EventDelivery.value` 时 `listener(value)` 接收原始 payload。两者返回 `R` 或 PromiseLike，监听器必须是函数。
默认 `EventDelivery.context`（`'context'`），保留 payload 与上下文控制；`EventDelivery.value`（`'value'`）直接传入原始 payload，不复制或包装。其他值抛 `INVALID_OPTIONS`。
默认 `undefined`，不设置任务标签。提供时必须是非空字符串；该值由订阅调用者命名，用于之后的任务选择。
同步按入口快照调用目标，不等待 Promise，也不返回监听器结果。快照内的监听器即使中途被退订或 `clear()`，仍收到本轮；新订阅留到之后的快照。
`taskId` 为订阅时设置的非空标签。返回只读选择视图 `IFilteredEventChannel`，交给并行、串行或 visitor 工具；视图没有订阅或发布方法，之后每次调用都会重新选择当前匹配项。
删除全部活动登记，不执行监听器内部的用户清理函数；默认 `removalPolicy: 'handle'` 下，旧取消句柄不会移除之后的新登记。
只读的当前活动登记数。空通道发布无操作，异步多目标调用得到空数组。

blocks.text: `unique` 模式下，重复订阅同一个监听器会得到控制同一代登记的句柄；只有首次取消生效。重复订阅的 `taskId` 和 delivery 必须与已有值相同，否则修改状态前抛 `INVALID_OPTIONS`；省略 delivery 与显式 `EventDelivery.context` 相同，省略 `taskId` 只匹配同样未设置的标签。`clear()` 或退订后重新订阅会创建新一代；`unique` 的句柄绑定原登记代，所以旧句柄不会取消新登记。Hub 和包装监听器的独立 helper 不按原始监听器身份去重。缺省 `multiple` 与 `removalPolicy: 'handle'` 组合下，每次登记可以分别取消。

不要把这种隔离套用于 `admissionPolicy: 'multiple'` 与 `removalPolicy: 'listener-all'` 的组合：尚未调用的旧句柄会按监听器函数身份移除当前全部匹配登记。即使先 `clear()`、再用同一个函数创建新登记，该旧句柄仍会移除它们。需要旧句柄与新登记隔离时，保留默认的 `handle` 移除策略；`unique` 则另有上述登记代绑定保证。

公开订阅选项类型为 `IEventSubscribeOptions`。默认/显式 context 重载使用 `IEventListener<T, R, V>`；显式 value 重载将原始 `T` 交给监听器，并接收 `R` 或 `PromiseLike<R>` 结果，必须提供 `{ delivery: EventDelivery.value }`。两种模式可在同一通道共存，调用工具沿用各自登记的模式和结果语义。
value 模式不附加 `abort()`、`aborted`、`abortReason`、`setTaskId()`、`taskId` 或 `valueConfig` 别名；payload 本身不被修改。登记标签仍可由 `filterTaskId()`、`invokeTask()` 选择。需要监听器内的取消、改标签或投影别名时保留默认 context。

rows: 本次发布的原始值，保持对象身份。
所属登记的实时取消状态与原因；进行中的回调也能读到更新。
发布入口快照中的任务标签，不随当前轮的改标签操作变化。
取消当前登记，原因默认 `undefined`。幂等；已经非活动时无操作，不中断已开始的回调。
接收非空字符串或 `undefined`；后者清除标签。只影响之后的快照，登记非活动时无操作。

blocks.text: `EventApiStyle` 导出四个预设：`subscribePublish`、`onEmit`、`onTrigger`、`listenFire`。需要跨模块比较或保存配置时使用这些常量。

自定义 `style` 是从语义到名字的对象，例如 `{ subscribe: 'observe', publish: 'dispatch', unsubscribe: 'dispose' }`。`style.subscribe` 和 `style.publish` 必填；`style.unsubscribe` 省略时为 `'unsubscribe'`。名字必须是非空字符串、彼此不同，不能占用另一语义的名字、`subscribeOnce`、`subscribeUntil`、`filterTaskId`、`clear`、`size` 或 `__proto__`、`prototype`、`constructor`。非法配置在构造时抛 `INVALID_OPTIONS`。
保留字面量配置可用 `as const satisfies IEventApiStyleNames`。显式给出 payload 类型后，自定义 channel style 也要在第三泛型 `S` 中提供；Hub 在第二泛型提供。宽化成普通 `string` 的对象不会产生任意方法名的索引签名。预设字面量有对应的推导重载。
canonical（固定的原名）方法始终存在；别名与原名指向同一函数，不创建另一个派发器。默认风格不增加别名属性；额外别名是不可枚举、不可写、不可配置的自有数据属性。style 不增加 `flush`、队列、排空、背压或跨进程能力。

`channel.subscribe()` 返回 `IEventChannelSubscription`，`hub.subscribe()` 返回 `IEventHubSubscription`。句柄本身可调用，`handle.unsubscribe === handle`；链式 `handle.subscribe(...)` 返回同一条链，风格的订阅别名与取消别名也保持函数身份。通道及句柄的 `subscribe`/订阅别名均接受 `taskId`、delivery 选项；Hub 及句柄的 `subscribe(key, listener, options?)`/订阅别名只接受 delivery，不接受 `taskId`。取消按追加顺序的逆序执行整条链，只真正执行一次。单个释放失败原样抛出；多个失败合为 `SUBSCRIPTION_DISPOSE_FAILED`，`AggregateError.errors` 保留执行顺序。关闭后追加订阅抛 `SUBSCRIPTION_CLOSED`。
链式扩展不是事务：后一次订阅失败时，前面成功的登记仍归原句柄所有，需要调用该句柄清理。第一条登记之后的句柄别名投影失败，则回滚该登记并以 `SUBSCRIPTION_HANDLE_PROJECTION_FAILED` 保留原始失败。有限字面量事件表在同一条 Hub 链上排除已经使用的 key；同 key 的另一条独立链仍可订阅。宽 key、索引签名或运行时联合 key 保留动态广播。

这些函数从 `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber` 导入，只要求结构兼容的 `channel.subscribe(listener, options?)`，不要求包内工厂身份。`subscribe` 必须返回函数，不能在安装尚未结束时同步交付事件；非法结构为 `INVALID_CHANNEL`。helper 保留对象方法的接收者。`subscribeOnce`、`subscribeUntil` 和对象订阅者保持 context-only，不接受 value 交付选项。

rows: 必填通道与函数；`options.taskId` 默认 `undefined`。第一次交付前先退订，所以同步重入、同步抛错或异步拒绝不会执行第二次。
必填通道、信号与函数；`options.taskId` 默认 `undefined`。信号取消时自动退订，手动退订也移除信号监听。取消不会中断已经开始的业务回调。
`subscriber` 必须是带可调用 `handle(event)` 的对象。`handle` 接收事件上下文，返回结果或 PromiseLike，并保留 `this`。缺少方法为 `INVALID_SUBSCRIBER`。

blocks.text: 返回值都是同步、幂等的 `IUnsubscribe`，不附加命名风格的 `off`、`dispose`、`unlisten` 或链式扩展。要使用带风格的订阅链，直接调用 channel 的订阅方法。

`subscribeUntil` 接受原生 `AbortSignal`，也接受具有布尔 `aborted`、可选 `reason`、可调用 `addEventListener` 与 `removeEventListener` 的兼容对象；事件类型固定为 `'abort'`。非法信号为 `INVALID_SIGNAL`。已取消信号默认不创建登记；只有 canonical channel 显式设置 `throwOnAborted: true` 时抛 `ABORTED`。
对象订阅者只需实现 `IEventSubscriber.handle(event)`。旧草案的抽象 `EventSubscriber`、静态 `EVENT_NAME`（也不是 `EVENTNAME`）与 `onCall()` 不属于当前公开契约：事件来源由传入的通道决定，多事件名称由 Hub 的订阅 key 决定，不重复保存在 class 中。
所有 `invoke*` 先同步固定目标快照，再开始等待。它们只接受同一份物理包实例创建的 canonical channel，或允许的 `filterTaskId()` 视图；伪造对象、Hub 或另一份包副本创建的通道为 `INVALID_CHANNEL`。参数 `value` 是本次交给每个监听器的值，无额外选项。

rows: 立即启动全部目标，等待全部结束，按登记顺序返回 `IListenerResult<R>[]`，与完成先后无关。监听器抛错和拒绝成为结果项。
调度相同；全部成功返回结果值数组，任一监听器失败则等全部结束后以 `PUBLISH_FAILED` 的 `AggregateError` 拒绝。
前一个目标结束后才启动下一个，失败后仍继续；返回按登记顺序的结算结果。
调度相同；失败后仍执行后面的目标，最后聚合抛出失败，全部成功返回结果值数组。
只接收 canonical channel；先精确选择一个任务，返回它的成功或失败结果。
精确选择相同；成功返回值，监听器失败以含一个原始失败的 `PUBLISH_FAILED` 拒绝。

blocks.text: 结算项为 `{ status: 'fulfilled', value: Awaited<R> }` 或 `{ status: 'rejected', reason: unknown }`。常量 `EventSubscriberState.fulfilled`、`rejected` 用于判断结果，`EventSubscriberState.abort` 是信号事件名。settled 只把监听器失败变成结果，不把非法通道或任务选择错误变成结果。
串行调用不是 waterfall：所有目标收到同一个原始值，前一个返回值不会传给下一个。异步工具通过返回值交付监听器失败，不再把同一个失败送给 `report`；值路径诊断仍遵循独立的诊断规则。
`taskId` 来自订阅时的 `options.taskId` 或之后的 `event.setTaskId()`，必须是非空字符串。入口匹配数为零时同步抛 `TASK_NOT_FOUND`；多于一个时同步抛 `TASK_NOT_UNIQUE`，都发生在任何目标被执行前。错误上有可枚举的 `taskId` 与 `matchCount`。任务不是全局注册表，标签只在传入通道内选择。

`withSnapshotEntries(channel, value, visitor)` 把本轮不可变 `IEventInvocation[]` 交给 visitor，由集成方决定调用顺序。`entry.taskId` 是快照标签，`entry.invoke()` 返回监听器原始结果或 PromiseLike，每个 entry 只准调用一次。visitor 可以同步返回或返回 Promise；它结束或拒绝后，全部 entry 关闭，之后调用抛 `INVOCATION_CLOSED`。visitor 同步抛出或异步拒绝以 `VISITOR_FAILED` 标识；可附码的原生错误保留身份和 stack，其余原值通过 `cause` 保留，entry 仍会关闭。
`invokeEachLive(channel, value, visitor)` 每次把一个 invocation 交给同步 visitor。在访问期间新追加的订阅也可以被本轮看到，每个登记最多访问一次。visitor 必须同步完成，抛错时内部遍历状态仍会释放，失败以 `VISITOR_FAILED` 标识。它只用于确实需要遍历期间看到新订阅的框架集成；普通业务优先选快照型工具。

`createEventHub<C, S, V>(options?)` 用事件表 `C` 关联 key 和 payload。options 只接受 `report`、`terminalReport`、`style`、`valueConfig`，默认值与含义同 channel；`report` 的参数额外带本次发布的 `key`。Hub listener 返回 `void` 或 `PromiseLike<void>`，不聚合结果；需要结果的事件另建 `createEventChannel<T, R>()`。

rows: key 是事件表中的字符串、数字或 symbol，listener 必须是函数。第三参只接受 delivery：默认/显式 `EventDelivery.context` 接收上下文，`EventDelivery.value` 接收该 key 的原始 payload；不接受 `taskId`。首次订阅该 key 时才创建内部 channel；返回可调用的订阅链。
只向该 key 分发对应类型的值；从未订阅或已经没有登记的 key 无操作，不会创建 channel。
指定 key 清除该事件所有登记并移除空 channel；省略时清除全部事件。
指定 key 返回该事件的活动登记数，不存在为零；省略返回总数。总数由计数器维护，不遍历所有 key。

blocks.text: 非法 key 为 `INVALID_EVENT_KEY`，非法 listener 为 `INVALID_LISTENER`。旧句柄不会取消 `clear()` 后新创建的同名事件登记。Hub 内部固定使用 `recursive`、`multiple`、`handle`、`100_000` 调用预算与非严格的已取消准入；不暴露内部 channel，也不接受单通道策略选项。需要自选这些策略时使用 channel。`EventRemovalPolicy.listenerAll` 适用于复用相同函数身份的整体注销，例如 logger hook 的注销路径。
`valueConfig` 在构造时固定路径，把原始 payload 中的一个值附加到 context 模式的上下文，同时保留原始 `event.value` 和所有控制方法。value 模式仍直接收到原始 payload，不附加别名。它不保存、转换或重放事件。

rows: 静态路径，类型为 `IObjectPath<T>` 或空字符串。空字符串或仅空白禁用整个投影；不读取 alias，不解析、不探测、不报告。
活动路径需要非空、无首尾空白的名字；不能与上下文成员或 `__proto__`、`prototype`、`constructor` 冲突。`resource` 不是保留名称。

blocks.text: 用 `as const` 或显式的 `V` 保留路径与 alias 字面量；channel 的 `V` 是第四泛型，Hub 的是第三泛型。每轮发布或调用只探测路径一次，全部目标得到同一个投影值身份。alias 为可枚举、不可写、不可配置的自有数据属性。
路径缺失、被阻断或 getter 抛错时，报告 `VALUE_PROJECTION_FAILED`；监听器仍调用，alias 为 `undefined`。实际存在且值为 `undefined` 的叶节点成功，不报告失败。原始 getter 错误保留在原因链中。没有目标时不探测路径。这里不支持函数 selector、transform、operator、fallback 或每个监听器再懒求值一次。
`publish()` 收集全部同步监听器失败后抛带 `PUBLISH_FAILED` 的 `AggregateError`；监听器返回的 Promise 在它返回后拒绝，则交给 `report`。同步发布不会因为迟到失败变成可等待的调用。
`report` 不存在或失败时，先尝试 `terminalReport`，再依次尝试宿主 `reportError`、`console.error`、排入微任务抛出；宿主不能排入微任务时同步抛出。报告函数本身的失败也保留在诊断错误链上，不静默丢弃。

包级错误的 `source` 为 `EVENT_SUBSCRIBER_SOURCE`，值是 `'event.subscriber'`。输入校验保留原生 `TypeError`，发布聚合保留 `AggregateError`。原始失败通过 `errors` 与 `cause` 可达；存在监听器失败时，`cause` 是第一个失败。只有预算耗尽时，`errors` 可以为空。业务代码比较 `EventSubscriberErrorCode` 的成员，不散写码值。`EventSubscriberErrorText` 是内部文案表，不是公开导出，业务代码不能导入；锁定文案时断言实际错误的 `message`。

snapshot 或 live visitor 抛错，或 snapshot visitor 异步拒绝。

blocks.text: `PUBLISH_FAILED` 时展开 `error.errors`，查看原始监听器失败；只有同步预算耗尽时可以没有监听器错误。任务选择失败时检查标签与登记寿命，不要把多目标当成“任选一个”。已关闭链需要新建订阅。Promise 失败只出现在 report 而不从 `publish()` 抛出时，先确认是否属于同步返回后的拒绝。

blocks.text: 中文
`@migaia/event-subscriber` delivers local events to listeners, with explicit rules for awaiting results, cancelling subscriptions and selecting exactly one handler.

items: The screen shows a newer value, then jumps back. A listener publishes recursively before the remaining listeners finish the older round.
A recipient is skipped, or a new subscriber sees an old event. Publication walks a callback array that listeners are mutating.
An old page keeps receiving updates. Requests share a cancellation signal, but the subscription has a separate, forgotten lifetime.
One failed handler also loses successful replies. Fire-and-forget notification is treated like an awaited call without per-listener settlement.
A save writes twice. Double mounting registers the same command twice, with no uniqueness check before invocation.

Nested updates can finish one round at a time. Recursive broadcasts can deliver a newer value before an older round finishes; explicit queued dispatch completes the current snapshot first, as the example shows with values 1 and 2.

Subscription changes leave current recipients intact. Walking a mutable array can skip or add recipients mid-delivery; an entry snapshot fixes the targets, and the example delays the new subscriber until the second round.

One cancellation signal also owns the subscription. Manual cancellation often stops a request but forgets its listener; `subscribeUntil` removes both the subscription and abort observer. The example ends with no registrations left.

A failure does not erase successful parallel results. Handling only an aggregate rejection can lose successful replies; `invokeParallelSettled` returns each value or failure in registration order. The example retains the successful value 6.

Ambiguous command targets are rejected before execution. Broadcasting or picking the first match can duplicate a write or hide duplicate registration; `invokeTask` requires exactly one match. The example performs no second save.

blocks.text: The root entry provides channels, the Hub and invocation helpers. Import standalone subscription helpers from `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber`. Its only runtime dependency is `@migaia/utils`; it needs neither DOM nor Node and declares `sideEffects: false`.

rows: Creates a single-event channel with snapshot and reentry rules.
Routes local notifications by event name and payload type.
Ties a subscription lifetime to a cancellation signal.
Awaits all listeners in parallel and retains every outcome.
Waits for each listener before starting the next.
Requires exactly one `taskId` match before execution.

blocks.text: In `createEventChannel<T, R>()`, `T` is the published payload type and `R` is the listener result type. Specifying a result type keeps the same channel subscription model and creates no global task registry.

Subscription has two signatures: `subscribe(listener, options?: { taskId?: string; delivery?: 'context' }): subscription` retains event contexts, with the original payload in `event.value`; `subscribe(listener, options: { taskId?: string; delivery: 'value' }): subscription` passes the original payload directly to the listener.

The public options type is `IEventSubscribeOptions`; mode constants are `EventDelivery.context` and `EventDelivery.value`. Optional `taskId` is a caller-chosen label for this registration. The returned subscription cancels its registrations and can extend the chain.
Select value delivery explicitly when only the payload is needed:

Value delivery preserves payload identity and provides no context members such as `abort()`, `setTaskId()` or `taskId`. A registration's `taskId` still supports task filtering. Keep default context delivery when context controls or `valueConfig` aliases are needed. Channel chains, naming aliases and the Hub's third subscribe argument accept the same delivery selection; the Hub accepts no task label. `subscribeOnce` and `subscribeUntil` still accept context listeners only.

Dynamic event names support runtime fan-out. A finite literal event map rejects repeated event names on the same subscription chain through its TypeScript types; a separate chain can still subscribe to that name.

Defaults are recursive synchronous dispatch, multiple independent registrations, handle-scoped removal, `100_000` listener calls per top-level publish, and non-strict already-aborted admission. Subscription changes, clear and retagging do not change the current snapshot; later invocations select targets anew.

Synchronous `publish()` does not await Promises. Synchronous throws become `PUBLISH_FAILED`; late rejection goes to report. Async helpers await settlement and deliver results or rejection. Settled helpers collect listener failures, while invalid channels and task admission still throw synchronously.

`invokeParallelSettled(channel, payload)` returns outcomes in registration order: the `value` in `{ status: 'fulfilled', value }` is the listener's awaited return value; the `reason` in `{ status: 'rejected', reason }` is its original thrown value or rejection reason. These fields describe listener execution, not message-send acknowledgments.

Subscription handles chain and cancel once in reverse order; closed chains cannot extend. Static `valueConfig` adds one path value to context delivery without transforming events or value listeners’ payloads.

With `style: 'on-emit'`, `channel.on(listener)` registers a listener and returns its subscription handle, while `channel.emit(value)` delivers value to the current snapshot under the selected dispatch policy. Under default handle-scoped removal, the handle's `off()` removes only the registrations it owns. `on`, `emit` and `off` are the same functions as `subscribe`, `publish` and `unsubscribe`, respectively; the canonical names remain available.

Import `subscribeOnce`, `subscribeUntil` and `subscribeSubscriber` from `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber`. They work only through `channel.subscribe(listener, options?)` without reading style configuration, so they also accept styled channels that retain this method. A styled channel adds naming aliases. Each helper returns a plain `IUnsubscribe`: a synchronous, idempotent cancellation function with no `off`, `dispose`, `unlisten` or chain methods.

An object subscriber only implements `handle(event)` from `IEventSubscriber<T, R>`. The channel supplied to `subscribeSubscriber(channel, subscriber)` determines the event source; a Hub's `subscribe(key, listener)` key determines the event name. The old draft's abstract `EventSubscriber` class, static `EVENT_NAME` and `onCall()` are outside the current public contract; event names are not repeated on subscriber classes.
The Hub fixes its internal channels to the default policies and accepts no channel policy configuration. It does not aggregate listener results; use a channel with a result type when results matter.

Events are transient notifications, without current state, replay, process transport, resource hosting, drain or backpressure. See the usage guide for every option, naming styles, static value paths, 19 error codes and build commands.

Find your scenario first, then consult the full contract. After installation, save any runnable example as its own `.ts` file and execute it with Node 24. The code is shared with the corresponding website scenario. See the README for module selection.

sections.heading: Deliver nested notifications after the current round

blocks.text: An update listener publishes another update before the other listeners see the first. Hand-written `recursive` callbacks can make a screen show the newer event and then overwrite it with the older one. The `queued` policy finishes the current registration snapshot before delivering the nested value, within the same synchronous `publish` call.
Output:

blocks.code:
record: 1
render: 1
record: 2
render: 2

blocks.text: Prints `record: 1`, `render: 1`, `record: 2`, `render: 2`, in that order. The nested event does not interrupt the current round. The default policy is `recursive`; `queued` delivery is explicit.

sections.heading: Change subscriptions without changing the current delivery

blocks.text: A listener removes another listener or installs a new one while an event is being delivered. Walking a mutable callback array can skip a recipient or deliver the current event to a new registration unexpectedly. `publish` takes one registration snapshot: changes affect later publishes, while the current snapshot still completes in registration order.
Output:

blocks.code: first 1 | second 1 | first 2 | added 2

blocks.text: Prints `first 1 | second 1 | first 2 | added 2`. Removing the second registration does not remove it from the first snapshot; the new registration first runs on the second `publish`.

sections.heading: Release a page subscription across several event names

blocks.text: A page listens for save and close events, but its cleanup forgets one event name and the old page keeps receiving updates. A typed hub routes each event to its own payload type. Chaining the page registrations returns one handle that releases the entire chain in reverse order.
Output:

blocks.code:
saved: order-1
closed: details
subscriptions left: 0

blocks.text: Prints `saved: order-1`, `closed: details`, then `subscriptions left: 0`. The `publish` after page cleanup prints nothing. One handle removes both registrations in this chain.

sections.heading: Stop page updates with its cancellation signal

blocks.text: A component starts several operations under one `AbortController` but its event subscription survives navigation. Hand-written abort listeners need both event unsubscription and abort-listener cleanup. `subscribeUntil` ties the registration to the signal and returns an idempotent manual unsubscribe for earlier cleanup.
Output:

blocks.code:
render: saved
subscriptions left: 0

blocks.text: Prints `render: saved`, then `subscriptions left: 0`. Aborting removes future deliveries; calling `stop` afterwards is harmless. An already-running listener is not interrupted, and an already-aborted signal registers nothing by default.

sections.heading: Keep successful results when another listener fails

blocks.text: An export asks several handlers for results. A rejected `Promise` can hide successful replies if the caller handles only one aggregate failure. `invokeParallelSettled` starts the captured listeners immediately and returns each success or failure in registration order, including the original failure reason. Invalid `channel` admission still throws synchronously.
Output:

blocks.code:
success: 6
failure: remote unavailable

blocks.text: Prints `success: 6`, then `failure: remote unavailable`. The second listener fails before the first resumes after its microtask, but the result array follows registration order and retains the successful value.

sections.heading: Wait for one handler before starting the next

blocks.text: A notification starts before a preceding asynchronous write has finished because `publish` does not wait for listener Promises. `invokeSerial` awaits one captured listener before starting the next. Each receives the same input rather than the previous result. The example logs stand in for a write and a notification.
Output:

blocks.code:
write: order-1
write complete
notify: order-1
results: written,notified

blocks.text: Prints `write: order-1`, `write complete`, `notify: order-1`, then `results: written,notified`. This controls order, not a transaction: a failed listener does not skip later listeners; failures are aggregated after all have run.

sections.heading: Reject duplicate command targets before doing any work

blocks.text: A command should run one save handler, but double mounting registers it twice and writes twice. `invokeTask` selects one `taskId` before invoking any listener. A missing name throws `TASK_NOT_FOUND`; duplicate matches throw `TASK_NOT_UNIQUE` with no handler called for that attempt. Other task names are not invoked.
Output:

blocks.code:
save result: 3
duplicate target: TASK_NOT_UNIQUE
save calls: 1

blocks.text: Prints `save result: 3`, `duplicate target: TASK_NOT_UNIQUE`, then `save calls: 1`. The ambiguous second attempt performs no extra save. A selected listener failure rejects with `PUBLISH_FAILED` while retaining its original error.

The root entry, `@migaia/event-subscriber`, exports channels, the Hub, invocation helpers, constants and public types. The `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber` subpath exports `subscribeOnce`, `subscribeUntil`, `subscribeSubscriber` and their subscription types. The only runtime dependency is `@migaia/utils`. The module needs neither DOM nor Node APIs and declares `sideEffects: false`.

A channel delivers events as they are published. It stores no current value and replays no history. A registration is one subscription and its cancellation ownership. A snapshot fixes the target list when an invocation starts. Use `@migaia/reactive` for current state or derived dependencies, `@migaia/middleware-pipeline` for a sequence that passes each result to the next step, `@migaia/lifecycle` or `@migaia/resource` for resource ownership, queues and backpressure, and `@migaia/rpc-host` + transport plugin for messages crossing Workers, windows or networks.

`createEventChannel<T, R, S, V>(options?)` creates a channel. `T` is the published payload, `R` is a listener's result and defaults to `void`, `S` is the naming style, and `V` is a static value-path configuration. Both `S` and `V` default to `undefined`. The public options type is `IEventChannelOptions<T, S, V>`. For projection types used only by inference, consult the published declarations and editor hints.

rows: Receives `{ event, error }`. Handles listener rejection after synchronous `publish()` returns, plus value-path diagnostics. May return synchronously or return a Promise. Without it, failure goes to terminal diagnostics. Synchronous listener throws are aggregated by `publish()` instead.
Receives the diagnostic error when `report` is absent, throws or rejects. May return synchronously or return a Promise. Its own failure continues to host diagnostics.
`'recursive'` immediately delivers a publish made inside a listener; `'queued'` finishes the current snapshot before delivering nested values. Constants: `EventDispatchPolicy.recursive` and `queued`.
`'multiple'` creates an independent registration on every subscribe; `'unique'` keeps one registration per listener function identity. Constants: `EventAdmissionPolicy.multiple` and `unique`.

`'handle'` removes the registration owned by this handle; `'listener-all'` removes every registration of that listener function on this channel. Constants: `EventRemovalPolicy.handle` and `listenerAll`.

Maximum listener calls within one top-level synchronous publish, including nested publishes. Must be a positive safe integer. Exhaustion stops expansion and throws `PUBLISH_FAILED`; `error.detail` records processed calls and the remaining budget.
`false` makes `subscribeUntil` return a no-op without registering against an already-aborted signal; `true` throws an `ABORTED` TypeError synchronously.
Adds method aliases to the existing operations. See the four presets and custom fields below; dispatch and cancellation semantics stay the same.
No alias is added by default. A configured static `readPath` and `alias` expose one payload value on the context; see Static value paths.

blocks.text: `options` must be an object, never `null` or an array. Malformed options produce `INVALID_OPTIONS`. Supplied `report` and `terminalReport` values must be callable or produce `INVALID_REPORTER`. An option getter's original failure remains reachable through the error chain.

rows: Adds a listener in registration order and returns a callable chain handle. By default `listener(event)` receives the context below; explicit `delivery: EventDelivery.value` calls `listener(value)` with the original payload. Both return `R` or a PromiseLike. The listener must be a function.

Defaults to `EventDelivery.context` (`'context'`), retaining the payload and context controls. `EventDelivery.value` (`'value'`) passes the original payload without copying or wrapping. Other values throw `INVALID_OPTIONS`.
Defaults to `undefined`, leaving the registration unlabelled. A supplied label must be a nonempty string named by the subscribing caller, for later task selection.

Calls the entry snapshot synchronously, without waiting for Promises or returning listener results. Removal or `clear()` during dispatch does not remove targets from this snapshot; additions belong to later snapshots.

Takes a nonempty subscription label and returns an opaque read-only `IFilteredEventChannel` for parallel, serial or visitor helpers. The view has no subscribe or publish method; each invocation selects current matching registrations anew.
Removes active registrations without running user cleanup inside listeners. With the default `removalPolicy: 'handle'`, old cancellation handles cannot remove later registrations.
Read-only active registration count. Publishing an empty channel does nothing; asynchronous multi-target invocation returns an empty array.

blocks.text: In `unique` mode, subscribing the same function again returns a handle controlling the existing registration generation. Only the first removal changes state. A duplicate subscription must use the same `taskId` and delivery or throws `INVALID_OPTIONS` before state changes. Omitted delivery equals explicit `EventDelivery.context`; an omitted `taskId` matches only an unset label. Resubscribing after removal or `clear()` creates a new generation. A `unique` handle stays bound to its original generation, so it cannot cancel the new registration. The Hub and helpers that register wrappers do not deduplicate the original listener identity. The default combination of `multiple` admission and `removalPolicy: 'handle'` gives each registration independent cancellation.

That isolation does not apply to `admissionPolicy: 'multiple'` combined with `removalPolicy: 'listener-all'`. An old handle that has not yet been called removes all current registrations of its listener function, including new registrations created with that function after `clear()`. Keep the default `handle` removal policy when old handles must not affect later registrations; `unique` separately provides the generation binding described above.

The public subscription options type is `IEventSubscribeOptions`. Default or explicit context overloads use `IEventListener<T, R, V>`. Explicit value overloads pass the original `T` to the listener, accept an `R` or `PromiseLike<R>` result, and require `{ delivery: EventDelivery.value }`. Both modes can coexist on one channel; invocation helpers retain each registration's mode and result semantics.

Value delivery adds no `abort()`, `aborted`, `abortReason`, `setTaskId()`, `taskId` or `valueConfig` alias; the payload itself is not modified. The registration label still supports `filterTaskId()` and `invokeTask()`. Keep default context delivery for cancellation, retagging or projected aliases inside a listener.

rows: The original published value, preserving object identity.
Live cancellation state and reason for this registration; a running callback can observe updates.
The task label captured in this invocation's snapshot, unaffected by retagging during the current invocation.
Cancels this registration. The reason defaults to `undefined`. Idempotent and a no-op after deactivation; it does not interrupt an already-running callback.
Accepts a nonempty string or `undefined` to remove the label. Affects later snapshots only; inactive registrations ignore it.

blocks.text: `EventApiStyle` exports `subscribePublish`, `onEmit`, `onTrigger` and `listenFire`. Use these constants when comparing or retaining configuration across modules.

A custom `style` maps semantic operations to names, for example `{ subscribe: 'observe', publish: 'dispatch', unsubscribe: 'dispose' }`. `style.subscribe` and `style.publish` are required; `style.unsubscribe` defaults to `'unsubscribe'`. Names must be nonempty, distinct strings. They cannot take another operation's canonical name, `subscribeOnce`, `subscribeUntil`, `filterTaskId`, `clear`, `size`, `__proto__`, `prototype` or `constructor`. Invalid configuration throws `INVALID_OPTIONS` during construction.

Preserve literal names with `as const satisfies IEventApiStyleNames`. When explicitly supplying a payload type, supply custom channel style `S` as the third generic parameter; for the Hub, use the second. An object widened to ordinary `string` does not grant an arbitrary method-name index signature. Literal presets have their own inference overloads.

Canonical methods always remain available. Each alias is the same function as its canonical method, rather than a second dispatcher. The default style adds no alias properties; additional aliases are non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable own data properties. Styles add no flush, queue, drain, backpressure or process transport.

`channel.subscribe()` returns `IEventChannelSubscription`; `hub.subscribe()` returns `IEventHubSubscription`. A handle is callable, and `handle.unsubscribe === handle`. Chained `handle.subscribe(...)` returns the same chain. Styled subscription and cancellation aliases preserve function identity too. Channel and handle subscribe methods or aliases accept both `taskId` and delivery options. Hub and Hub-handle `subscribe(key, listener, options?)` methods or aliases accept only delivery, without `taskId`. Cancellation runs every disposer in reverse append order and executes only once. A single disposal failure is rethrown unchanged; several produce `SUBSCRIPTION_DISPOSE_FAILED` with original failures in execution order on `AggregateError.errors`. Extending a closed chain throws `SUBSCRIPTION_CLOSED`.

Chain extension is not transactional: if a later subscription fails, earlier registrations still belong to the original handle and must be cleaned up through it. Failure while projecting the first handle's aliases rolls back that registration and preserves the original failure under `SUBSCRIPTION_HANDLE_PROJECTION_FAILED`. A finite literal event map excludes keys already used on the same Hub chain; a separate chain may still subscribe to that key. Wide keys, index signatures and runtime union keys preserve dynamic fan-out.

Import these functions from `@migaia/event-subscriber/subscriber`. They require only a structurally compatible `channel.subscribe(listener, options?)`, not factory identity. The method must return a cancellation function and must not deliver an event synchronously before installation finishes; an invalid source produces `INVALID_CHANNEL`. Object method receivers are preserved. `subscribeOnce`, `subscribeUntil` and object subscribers remain context-only; they accept no value delivery option.

rows: Requires a channel and function. `options.taskId` defaults to `undefined`. Removes the subscription before its first callback, so synchronous reentry, a throw or a rejected Promise cannot run it twice.

Requires a channel, signal and function. `options.taskId` defaults to `undefined`. Signal cancellation removes the subscription; manual unsubscribe also removes the signal listener. Cancellation does not interrupt a running callback.
Requires an object with callable `handle(event)`. It receives the event context, may return a result or PromiseLike, and retains `this`. A missing method produces `INVALID_SUBSCRIBER`.

blocks.text: All return a synchronous, idempotent `IUnsubscribe`, without styled `off`, `dispose`, `unlisten` aliases or chain extension. Use the channel's own subscription method for styled chains.

`subscribeUntil` accepts native `AbortSignal` or a compatible object with boolean `aborted`, optional `reason`, and callable `addEventListener` and `removeEventListener` methods. The event type is `'abort'`. Invalid signals produce `INVALID_SIGNAL`. Already-aborted signals create no registration by default; a canonical channel explicitly configured with `throwOnAborted: true` throws `ABORTED`.

Object subscribers need only `IEventSubscriber.handle(event)`. The old draft's abstract `EventSubscriber`, static `EVENT_NAME` (nor `EVENTNAME`) and `onCall()` are outside the current API. The supplied channel determines the source. Hub subscription keys determine event names; subscriber classes do not repeat that information.

Every `invoke*` helper fixes its target snapshot synchronously before waiting. These helpers accept a canonical channel created by the same physical module instance, or an allowed `filterTaskId()` view. A fabricated object, Hub or channel from another module copy produces `INVALID_CHANNEL`. `value` is the value delivered to each listener; there is no extra options argument.

rows: Starts all targets immediately, waits for every settlement, and returns `IListenerResult<R>[]` in registration order, independent of completion order. Listener throws and rejections become result items.
Same scheduling. Returns values when all succeed; on any listener failure, waits for every target before rejecting with a `PUBLISH_FAILED` AggregateError.
Starts each target after the previous one settles, continuing after failure. Returns settlements in registration order.
Same scheduling, including continuing after failure. Throws aggregated failures at the end, or returns values when all succeed.
Accepts only a canonical channel, selects exactly one task, and returns its successful or failed settlement.
Same exact selection. Returns the successful value, or rejects with `PUBLISH_FAILED` containing the one original listener failure.

blocks.text: A settlement is `{ status: 'fulfilled', value: Awaited<R> }` or `{ status: 'rejected', reason: unknown }`. Compare `EventSubscriberState.fulfilled` and `rejected` for result status; `EventSubscriberState.abort` is the signal event name. Settled helpers turn listener failures into values, but invalid channels and task selection still throw synchronously.

Serial invocation is not a waterfall. Every listener gets the same original payload, not the previous result. These helpers deliver listener failures through return values or rejection rather than also sending them to `report`. Value-path diagnostics retain their separate reporting behavior.

`taskId` comes from subscription `options.taskId` or a later `event.setTaskId()` and must be a nonempty string. Zero matches throw `TASK_NOT_FOUND` synchronously; multiple matches throw `TASK_NOT_UNIQUE`, both before any target executes. The error has enumerable `taskId` and `matchCount` fields. Tasks are labels within the supplied channel, not a global task registry.

`withSnapshotEntries(channel, value, visitor)` gives the visitor an immutable `IEventInvocation[]` for this call. The integration chooses invocation order. `entry.taskId` is the captured label; `entry.invoke()` returns the listener's raw result or PromiseLike and may be called only once. The visitor may finish synchronously or return a Promise. When it returns or settles, every entry closes; later calls throw `INVOCATION_CLOSED`. A visitor throw or rejection receives `VISITOR_FAILED`. Attachable native errors retain identity and stack; other original values remain on `cause`. Entries close on failure too.

`invokeEachLive(channel, value, visitor)` gives a synchronous visitor one invocation at a time. New subscriptions appended during visitation may join this traversal; each registration is visited at most once. The visitor must finish synchronously. A throw still releases internal traversal state and receives `VISITOR_FAILED`. Use this only for framework integrations that require append visibility. Ordinary application code should use snapshot helpers.

sections.heading: Routing multiple events with a Hub

blocks.text: `createEventHub<C, S, V>(options?)` links keys to payloads through event map `C`. Its options are only `report`, `terminalReport`, `style` and `valueConfig`, with the same defaults and meanings as channels. The report argument also includes the published `key`. Hub listeners return `void` or `PromiseLike<void>`; results are not aggregated. Create a separate `createEventChannel<T, R>()` when an event needs results.

rows: The event-map key is a string, number or symbol, and the listener must be a function. The third argument accepts only delivery: default or explicit `EventDelivery.context` receives the context; `EventDelivery.value` receives that key’s original payload. It accepts no `taskId`. Creates an internal channel only for the first subscription to a key. Returns a callable chain.
Delivers the correctly typed value only to this key. An unregistered key does nothing and creates no channel.
A supplied key removes all its registrations and its empty channel. Omitting the key clears all events.
A supplied key returns its active count, or zero if absent. Omission returns the total, maintained by a counter without traversing every key.

blocks.text: Invalid keys produce `INVALID_EVENT_KEY`; invalid listeners produce `INVALID_LISTENER`. Old handles cannot cancel newly recreated registrations after `clear()`. Internal Hub channels fix recursive dispatch, multiple admission, handle removal, a `100_000` invocation budget and non-strict aborted admission. The Hub exposes neither its channels nor channel policy options. Use a channel to select those policies. `EventRemovalPolicy.listenerAll` supports whole-function removal where a caller reuses the same listener identity, including logger hook unregistration.

`valueConfig` fixes a path at construction and adds that payload value to context delivery while preserving the original `event.value` and all controls. Value delivery still receives the original payload without an alias. It stores, transforms and replays no events.

rows: A static `IObjectPath<T>` or empty string. Empty or whitespace-only paths disable the entire projection before reading alias, parsing, probing or reporting.
An active path requires a nonempty name with no leading or trailing whitespace. It cannot collide with context members, `__proto__`, `prototype` or `constructor`. `resource` is not reserved.

blocks.text: Preserve path and alias literals with `as const` or explicit `V`: the channel's fourth generic parameter and the Hub's third. Each publish or invocation probes the path once, sharing the projected value's identity across all targets. The alias is an enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable own data property.

Missing or blocked paths and getter failures report `VALUE_PROJECTION_FAILED`; listeners still run with an `undefined` alias. A present leaf whose value is `undefined` is successful and does not report. Original getter failures remain on the cause chain. No targets means no path probe. Function selectors, transforms, operators, fallbacks and lazy per-listener projection are unsupported.

`publish()` attempts the synchronous listener snapshot, collects its throws, then throws a `PUBLISH_FAILED` AggregateError. A returned Promise rejecting after the call returns goes to `report`. Late failure does not make synchronous publishing awaitable.

If `report` is absent or fails, diagnostics try `terminalReport`, then host `reportError`, `console.error`, and a queued microtask throw. Without microtask support, the final throw is synchronous. Failures of reporters remain in the diagnostic error chain; they are not silently dropped.

module errors use `EVENT_SUBSCRIBER_SOURCE`, whose value is `'event.subscriber'`, as their `source`. Admission preserves native `TypeError`; publication aggregation preserves `AggregateError`. Original failures remain reachable through `errors` and `cause`. With listener failures, `cause` is the first failure. Budget-only failure may have an empty `errors` array. Compare `EventSubscriberErrorCode` members instead of scattering code strings. `EventSubscriberErrorText` is an internal message table, not a public export; application code must not import it. To lock down user-facing text, assert the actual error's `message`.

blocks.text: For `PUBLISH_FAILED`, inspect `error.errors` for original listener failures. A synchronous budget failure can occur without listener errors. For task selection failure, check labels and registration lifetimes instead of choosing an arbitrary duplicate. Closed chains need a new subscription. If a Promise failure appears only in report, check whether rejection happened after synchronous `publish()` returned.
